projects.title: Parallax Census
projects.tagline: A local-first registry for projects, artifacts, sources, aliases, relationships, evidence states, and custody receipts.
projects.story: Parallax Census helps the Archive discover and organize the growing body of Parallax work without confusing discovery with ownership, consent, truth, uniqueness, or permission to publish. Candidate records pass through normalization, provenance, custody, duplicate, privacy, freshness, claim-boundary, and human-authority review before any canonical change is allowed.
projects.summary: A project-and-artifact registry architecture preserving local control, deterministic validation, custody, quarantine, aliases, supersession, withdrawal, and explicit human approval. It is not a population census, identity system, surveillance platform, web crawler, or automatic publisher.
projects.see: The Census cover, registry lifecycle, consent-and-provenance gate, architecture and boundary briefs, fixed-data Registry Workbench, source lineage, relationships, planned portable schema, and the next audited ingestion proof.
projects.proof: Seven public artifacts are connected. The fixed-data Workbench deterministically distinguishes a clean public candidate, exact duplicate, alias collision, private source, stale canonical state, and orphan artifact while performing no personal-data intake, crawling, persistence, model calls, or Archive mutation.
projects.next: Freeze a portable versioned registry schema and import/export manifest, then run the first audited ingestion across the existing Archive pack files. Publish candidate counts, aliases, duplicate findings, missing provenance, consent states, accepted changes, rejected changes, and custody receipts without silently mutating canonical records.
projects.claimBoundary: This package demonstrates registry architecture, public explanation, deterministic fixed synthetic review logic, and Archive integration. It does not prove complete discovery, legal ownership, authorship, copyright permission, authenticity, consent, claim truth, absence of duplicates, public-release authority, or that omitted work does not exist. Census is a project-and-artifact registry, not a population census or identity-profiling system. Every real canonical change requires explicit human approval and a versioned receipt.
